EXECUTIVE ORDER 9260 
L e g io n o f M e r it
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by section 2 of the 
act of July 20, 1942 (Public Law 671—  
77th Congress), I  hereby prescribe the 
following rules and regulations for the 
award of the decoration of the “Legion 
of Merit” created by said act:
1. The decoration of the Legion of 
Merit shall be awarded by the President 
of the United States or at his direction to 
members of the armed forces of the 
United States and of the Government of 
the Commonwealth of the Philippines, 
and members of the armed forces of 
friendly foreign nations, who, after the 
proclamation of an emergency by the 
President on September 8, 1939,1  shall 
have distinguished themselves by excep­
tionally meritorious conduct in the per­
formance of outstanding services.
2. Awards of the decoration of the Le­
gion of Merit may be proposed to the 
President by the Secretary of War and 
by the Secretary of the Navy, each acting 
upon the recommendation of an officer 
of the armed forces of the United States 
who has personal knowledge of the serv­
ices of the person recommended.
3. Recommendations for awards to 
members of the armed forces of friendly 
foreign nations shall be submitted to the 
President of the United States for his 
approval.

research_rationale:
EO 9260 (October 29, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt; 7 FR 8819) was read in full in the held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9260.txt). Acting under section 2 of the act of July 20, 1942, it prescribes three numbered rules for the Legion of Merit: (1) award by the President or at his direction to members of the armed forces of the United States, the Commonwealth of the Philippines and friendly foreign nations for exceptionally meritorious conduct after the proclamation of an emergency on September 8, 1939; (2) awards may be proposed to the President by the Secretaries of War and of the Navy on the recommendation of an officer with personal knowledge; (3) recommendations for awards to members of friendly foreign armed forces go to the President for approval. The provisional status is no and is adopted. Amendment: Executive Order 10600 (March 15, 1955, 20 FR 1569) amended paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 to read as follows; that is a later event for each clause, not an end. Executive Order 10599, printed on the same Federal Register page, concerns an acting judge in Puerto Rico and does not touch this order. First end: Executive Order 13830 of April 20, 2018 (83 FR 18191, Federal Register issue of April 25, 2018), section 8(c), states that it supersedes Executive Order 4601 of March 1, 1927, as amended, and Executive Order 9260 of October 29, 1942, as amended. Section 4 of 13830 restates the Legion of Merit rules (award by the service Secretaries, degrees for foreign members by the Secretary of Defense, Chief Commander recommendations to the President), so the supersession is an express, named replacement of all three paragraphs. 13830 states no later effective date; the date recorded is its signing date, April 20, 2018, with publication on April 25, 2018 noted. Selden leads: I used the Selden citer lead for EO 13830 (FR Doc. 2018-08883) only as a pointer; the ending is cited from the producer-registered full text of 13830 held in the repository, and I read the whole order, including the proviso keeping existing regulations in effect. The bounded Federal Register full-text search for Executive Order 9260 (1994 to 2026-10-14) found one document, 13830, and no other acting instrument. The ending would have been possible without the Selden text because the dossier already carried the 13830 provision through the act-of-supersession lead and the full text is held in jobs/fr-originals. Counterevidence: held texts citing 9260 by number are 10600 (twice, as the same Federal Register page), 13830, the 1989 OFR codification entry and the library-survey page; none revokes or reinstates it earlier than 13830. Source note: the order text relied on is the Federal Register text layer held in the repository (machine-extracted from the official PDF; the PDF itself is not held, only its hash). It was read in full; identity (number, date, subject, signature) was confirmed from that text. No page image was inspected.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 13830 section 8(c) keeps existing regulations prescribed under Executive Orders 4601 and 9260 in effect, so far as not inconsistent with 13830, until modified or revoked by regulations of the Secretary of the military department concerned (or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard); those regulations are separate instruments and survive the supersession. Section 8(d) of 13830 also provides that it does not invalidate any award of military decorations made before its effective date, so Legion of Merit awards made under the order are accrued effects. Neither survival keeps any command of EO 9260 itself operative after April 20, 2018.
